key_insight: TurboVLA rethinks vision-language-action policies by removing the heavy LLM-centric pipeline and mapping visual plus language inputs directly to actions. This enables real-time robot control at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 while using less than 1 GB of VRAM.
problem_solved: Standard VLA models are often too slow and memory-hungry for real-time robotics because they route every decision through a large language model, creating high compute and VRAM overhead.
method: Reformulates the traditional V -> L -> A pipeline into a direct V + L -> A mapping.
Avoids repeatedly projecting visual inputs into an LLM representation space for every policy call.
Targets efficient inference for robot control, balancing latency, memory use, and action quality.
impact: This approach makes VLA models more practical for robotics and edge deployment, where fast response times and limited GPU memory are critical. It lowers the barrier for running advanced multimodal policies in real time on single consumer GPUs.

paper_title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
paper_authors: Hengyi Xie, Chenfei Yao, Xianjin Wu, Xuanyang Xi, Yiping Tang
